context: Educational, non-combat civil-protection quiz. No weapons, harm or combat content.

questions.question: An official flood warning is issued for your area. What is the right way to treat it?

options.text: As real, and act on it without waiting to see the water
As a possible false alarm until the water reaches your street
As information for people who live next to the river only
As something to confirm by phoning neighbours first

questions.why: A warning means flooding is expected, and water can rise faster than people expect.

questions.question: Which item belongs in a grab bag you can pick up in seconds?

options.text: Copies of important documents in a waterproof bag
A full set of kitchen tools
Perishable food for a week
A large electrical appliance

questions.why: Documents and medicines matter more than heavy belongings, and the bag must be quick to carry.

questions.question: About how deep can moving water be before it can knock an adult off their feet?

options.text: About 15 cm
About 60 cm
About 1 metre
Only above chest height

questions.why: Even shallow moving water is dangerous, and its depth and force cannot be judged by looking.

questions.question: Which of these is a danger of floodwater?

options.text: Hidden holes and debris under the surface
It is always clean if it looks clear
It is always calm when the surface is calm
It never reaches a building's electrics

questions.why: Floodwater hides hazards, can be contaminated even when clear, and can move with force.

questions.question: True or false: it is safe to drive through floodwater if the water looks shallow.

options.text: True
False

questions.why: Moving water about 30 cm deep can float a car, and the real depth cannot be judged by looking.

questions.question: What comes first when a flood warning is issued?

options.text: Move to higher ground at once, alone
Listen to the official instructions
Check the electrics
Photograph the street

questions.why: Start from the official instructions, then gather and support people, and move before the water arrives.

questions.question: You have two routes to higher ground. Which one do you choose?

options.text: A longer route that stays above the water
The shortest route, even through shallow water
Whichever route has the fewest people on it
A route along the river bank

questions.why: A longer dry route is safer than a shorter one through floodwater.

questions.question: Why do you point at one named person when asking them to call 112?

options.text: It is quicker to speak to fewer people
A general request leads people to assume someone else has called
Only one person can use a phone at a time
Emergency services take calls from named people only

questions.why: Naming one person avoids everyone assuming that someone else has already called.

questions.question: When should you return to a building after a flood?

options.text: When the authorities say the area is safe
As soon as the water drops below the door
When you see other people going back in
After you have switched on the lights to check

questions.why: Water may still be high in places and structures and electrics may be unsafe.

questions.question: Which of these is a right action after a flood?

options.text: Pump out a flooded basement as quickly as possible
Switch the electrics on to check them
Treat tap water as unsafe until it is announced as safe
Go back in as soon as the water drops below the door

questions.why: Water and electrics need checking, damage records help later, and fast pumping can damage walls and floors.
